name: PT Indonesia Prima Property Tbk

frontmatter.title: An asset-rich, cash-poor land bank priced above the value we can evidence
frontmatter.summary: OMRE owns a Bandung mall, hotel and apartment assets and a large Bali land bank carried at historical cost. The operating businesses lose money, the land has never been appraised, and the shares trade above any asset value we can evidence. We rate the stock SELL with a target of Rp465, -48.1% from the last price, after the land-appraisal discount and the marketability haircut.
thesis: Asset value, not earnings, is the only defensible anchor: land at carrying cost of IDR2,052.1bn, the Aurora joint venture at IDR1,326.4bn and the Westin Nusa Dua associate at IDR126.4bn [S7].
The operating shell burns cash: revenue of IDR42.8bn against G&A of IDR139.4bn and a net result of IDR-183.5bn in FY2025 [S7].
The funding gap is closed by interest-free related-party payables, which rose from IDR553.3bn to IDR668.5bn in the nine months to September 2026 [S8].
Concentration is extreme: 78.4% of the register sits with two holders and the free float is 21.6%, so the shares trade on a daily value of IDR14.4m [S7][S0].
Even on our asset value the shares are not cheap: RNAV-based value is Rp629 against a last price of Rp895, and the market already pays 0.8x its book value [S0][S7].

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results and the dividend decision, the first full year showing whether the mall and hotel repositioning earns anything
Annual general meeting; any land-disposal authority or related-party mandate is voted here
Expected reopening of the renovated Grand Tropic Suites hotel in Surabaya, which management gives no firm date for
Any signed sale of Bali land at Antap or Ubud, or a launch of the Aurora joint venture land, would be the first external evidence of value

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Indonesia Prima Property (OMRE) with a SELL rating and a twelve-month target of Rp465, which is -48.1% from the last price of Rp895 [S0]. OMRE is not a developer in any operating sense. It is a small, thinly traded owner of a Bandung shopping centre, hotel and apartment assets, a residential parcel in Tangerang and a large Bali land bank, administered from a single Jakarta office with 218 staff [S7].

Our difference with the market is in how the assets are counted, not in the operating forecast. The market pays 0.8x stated book value for land that has never been revalued and for a joint venture carried at more than the group's share of its audited equity because advances were capitalised into the carrying amount [S7]. We value the land at the carrying cost the financial statements disclose, capitalise the recurring rent at the appraiser's own discount rate, carry the joint venture and associate at book, bring in every other balance-sheet asset and deduct every liability and the minority, and then apply the land-appraisal discount the method card requires for unappraised raw land, followed by the house marketability haircut for this register [S7]. That gives an RNAV-based value of Rp629 per share before liquidity, and a target of Rp465 once the marketability haircut is applied [S0].

Two events would change the view, and neither is in the current numbers. A signed sale of a Bali parcel, or a sale by the Aurora joint venture of its own land, would convert unappraised cost into evidence and could justify a materially narrower discount [S7]. A recovery in Bandung mall and Surabaya hotel occupancy toward the levels the appraiser assumes would raise the capitalised-rent component of our asset value [S7]. Until either happens, the shares are a leveraged bet on an appraisal nobody has published.

The balance sheet is not distressed in the conventional sense: at 30 September 2026 the group held cash of IDR15.8bn against bank loans of IDR3.7bn, and parent equity was IDR3,181.3bn [S8]. But the operating businesses lose money and the gap is funded by interest-free related-party payables, which rose from IDR553.3bn at the end of FY2025 to IDR668.5bn at 30 September 2026 [S8]. That is a shareholder subsidy rather than a business model, and it is the most important fact about the quality of this equity [S7][S8].

OMRE is the listed vehicle for the Indonesian property interests of First Pacific Capital Group Limited, whose ultimate beneficial owners the annual report names as Michelle Liem Mei Fung and Tan Enk Ee [S7]. Two holders dominate the register: First Pacific Capital Group holds 1,295.5m shares and PT Manning Development, an entity controlled by key management personnel, holds 1,014.0m, together 78.4% of the 2,945.2m shares in issue, leaving a free float of 21.6% [S7][S0].

The portfolio is small and old-economy. Plaza Parahyangan, a Bandung retail landmark trading for four decades and managed by subsidiary PT Almakana Sari, is the largest single income asset and is carried at an appraised fair value of IDR108.5bn [S7]. The group also owns hotel and serviced-apartment assets, including Grand Tropic Suites in Surabaya, a residential project at Bukit Tiara in Cikupa, Tangerang, and undeveloped land in Bali at Antap and Ubud [S7].

The land is the reason to look at the company. Its carrying value is IDR2,052.1bn, of which IDR1,791.2bn sits in Bali and IDR237.9bn at Bukit Tiara [S7]. The hectares are large relative to the revenue they produce: 1,688,281 square metres at Bukit Tiara, 468,760 square metres at Antap and 1,032,690 square metres at Ubud [S7]. None of it is revalued, none of it is appraised, and the annual report gives no sale timetable for any parcel [S7].

The revenue mix reflects that history. FY2025 revenue was IDR42.8bn, of which the residential segment contributed IDR3.3bn; the balance is rent from the mall, the apartments and the hotel [S7]. Occupancy is the operative fact for the recurring business: 53.0% at Plaza Parahyangan, 31.5% in the apartments and 33.0% across the hotel's 188 rooms [S7]. A shopping centre half empty produces rent, but it does not produce pricing power.

Management's disclosed strategy is to reposition what it already owns rather than build. The annual report describes the renovation of Plaza Parahyangan, the intended reopening of the Surabaya hotel as a modern tropical address, and the sale of Bali land in kavling plots when buyers appear [S7]. There is no marketing-sales target and no presales disclosure of the kind a residential developer would publish, which is itself informative: the group does not run a development pipeline it can forecast, and the quarterly filings contain no bookings metric [S7][S8].

The largest asset after the land is the Aurora Development joint venture. The group carries its interest at IDR1,326.4bn, which is above its half share of the vehicle's IDR2,501.2bn of attributable equity because advances to the vehicle were capitalised into the carrying amount [S7]. The vehicle itself holds investment properties of IDR1,412.0bn and development properties of IDR1,680.7bn, and its comprehensive loss in FY2025 was IDR-121.9bn [S7]. A separate associate, PT Nusadua Graha International, which holds the Westin Nusa Dua interest, is 26.7% owned and carried at IDR126.4bn [S7]. The two vehicles together are the part of the group with real Bali development exposure, and neither is consolidated line by line in a way that lets an outsider mark it.

In competitive terms OMRE is a challenger by default. It is a micro-cap with single-city retail exposure, no brand through which to charge tenants a premium, and a Bandung position that rests on a building's location in the distro district rather than on a franchise or a loyalty base [S7]. Its scale in Bali land is meaningful locally but invisible nationally, and its operating business is smaller than that of any listed peer we cover in the sector [S7][S0].

Property income in Indonesia is a rate trade, and the rate has stopped helping. Bank Indonesia held its policy rate at its October 2026 meeting, and the house macro deck carries the policy rate at 5.8% across the forecast years, with CPI at 3.3% and real GDP growth at 5.3% [S10][deck]. Stable rates are not the same as easy money: the deck has no cut in it, so the cap-rate compression that would re-rate a mall landlord is not in our forecast [deck].

The second transmission channel is the currency. The deck carries USD/IDR at 18,350 for FY2027E against a spot of 18,190, with a long-run rate of 19,000 [deck]. A weaker rupiah raises the cost of any imported fit-out and hotel consumables, and it makes a Bali holiday cheaper for the foreign visitor the island depends on [S10][S9]. For a landlord whose tenants are local retailers, the currency matters mainly through imported inventory and through the purchasing power of the tourist segment.

Bali is the group's land-bank story and its weakest demand signal. Foreign arrivals to the island fell again in September 2026, and the provincial statistics office described the drop as seasonal, with a pattern close to the two preceding years [S9]. Seasonal or not, arrivals that fail to grow cap the price a kavling buyer will pay for Ubud or Antap land, and they cap hotel room rates while the Surabaya property is still closed for renovation [S9][S7].

The retail side is a story of occupancy rather than rent. Plaza Parahyangan runs at 53.0% occupancy, which is what a market with newer competing centres produces for a building of that vintage [S7]. Tenant bargaining power in a half-empty mall is close to absolute: tenants can negotiate turnover-linked rents or simply move to a newer centre, and the landlord's response is capital spending on refurbishment rather than rent increases [S7]. That is the mechanism behind the renovation the annual report describes.

On Porter's five forces, the picture is unattractive on four of them. Buyer power is high because occupancy is low and tenants are mobile [S7]. Rivalry is high because Bandung retail supply has grown while the addressable market has not [S7]. The threat of substitutes comes from e-commerce and from out-of-town retail, which we discuss as background rather than as a sourced claim about this company's tenants. Supplier power is moderate: contractors are plentiful, but a listed landlord with a single mall has little leverage on price [S7]. The one force that helps is the threat of new entrants into the specific land the group holds: Ubud and Antap parcels of that size are not replaceable at cost [S7].

The moat, such as it is, is land scarcity in Bali and a location in Bandung that cannot be recreated. Neither is monetised. A moat that produces no pricing power is a balance-sheet asset, not an earnings moat, which is exactly why we value this company on RNAV rather than on a multiple of profits [S7].

Indonesian retail property has been through a decade in which new mall supply in the major cities outran household income growth, and older centres without refurbishment lost tenants to newer formats. Tourism-dependent island markets such as Bali recover faster than domestic retail because the demand is external, but they are also more exposed to global travel cycles, airline capacity and visa policy. Land held at historical cost can sit on a balance sheet for decades without producing income, and the value only becomes visible when a transaction occurs.

The revenue line has more than halved. Revenue went from IDR88.3bn in FY2022 to IDR71.4bn, then IDR63.5bn and IDR42.8bn in FY2025, a year in which revenue growth was -32.5% [S0]. The company's own explanation for the FY2025 drop is a fall of 32.6% against the prior year, driven by the handover of Mal Blok M back to the DKI Jakarta government and the closure of the Surabaya hotel [S7]. Both causes are permanent rather than cyclical: the mall is no longer the company's, and the hotel is closed pending renovation, so the lost revenue does not come back with occupancy [S7]. The nine months to September 2026 were flat against the prior year at IDR30.4bn, so the decline has stopped but has not reversed [S8].

The cost structure is the problem, and it is structural. FY2025 gross profit was IDR13.0bn, a gross margin of 30.3%, against G&A of IDR139.4bn [S7]. EBIT was IDR-123.4bn and EBITDA IDR-118.9bn, so the company loses money before it pays for its balance sheet [S7]. The headcount of 218 against revenue of IDR42.8bn is the arithmetic of that gap: this is a company whose overhead was built for a much larger business [S7].

We restate two lines from the filing because the data pack is wrong on both. Depreciation and amortisation for FY2025 is IDR4.5bn in the segment note, while the only depreciation figure the pack carries is the IDR3.2bn charged inside administrative expenses, so the pack understates the real charge by the difference between the two [S7]. Capex is restated the same way: total additions including investment properties were IDR6.7bn in FY2025 and IDR7.8bn in FY2024, against a cash-flow line in the pack that captures only purchases of property and equipment and therefore misses the investment-property additions [S7]. Both restatements are in the model and both are flagged for review, and both make free cash flow look worse, not better.

Working capital is the balance-sheet fact that defines the company. Reported operating working capital at the end of FY2025 was IDR-548.7bn, deeply negative because customer advances and related-party payables exceed current assets [S0][S7]. The pack's current liabilities include IDR553.3bn of interest-free related-party payables, which the group uses to fund the operating deficit; that balance rose to IDR668.5bn by 30 September 2026 [S8]. Funding a loss-making landlord with shareholder money is not a going-concern problem while the shareholder keeps funding it, but it does mean that reported losses understate the cash the business consumes and that the equity is not self-sustaining [S8].

Our forecast is deliberately close to the last actual. Revenue is held broadly flat in FY2026 at IDR42.8bn because the nine-month run rate is flat, then grows 4.0% in FY2027E and between 5.0% and 4.0% thereafter as the renovated mall re-leases and the hotel reopens, reaching IDR50.4bn by FY2030E [S7][S8]. Gross margin is held at 30.3%, the FY2025 level, because there is no evidence that the mix changes [S7].

Overhead is kept where it is in the accounts. G&A stays in operating cost at 339.0% of revenue, the level the audited year carries, and it grows with revenue at nominal rates rather than being held flat or reclassified below the EBITDA line [S7]. On that basis FY2026E revenue of IDR42.8bn carries G&A of IDR144.9bn, EBITDA of IDR-127.2bn and a net loss of IDR-126.4bn, which is the annualised run rate of the IDR-91.2bn nine-month loss the company actually reported [S8]. The only non-operating item we carry is the interest the LK shows on the Aurora receivable, IDR5.9bn, because the template's interest-income line reads the modelled cash balance and that balance is an artefact of the working-capital clamp discussed below [S7]. We do not forecast a return to profit: the G&A base is larger than the gross profit the asset base can generate at any plausible occupancy.

The forecast balance sheet contains one artefact that a reader must understand. The template caps operating working capital at -100.0% of revenue, while the company actually runs at a far larger negative, so the first forecast year shows a mechanical outflow as the model releases the related-party funding that the real balance sheet retains [S0]. That is why the cash line reads IDR9.8bn at FY2025 and IDR-625.4bn in FY2026E, and why net debt prints IDR640.7bn [S0]. It is a modelling limitation, not a forecast of an overdraft: the group funds itself through the payables above, and our valuation uses the reported balance sheet at 30 September 2026 rather than this line [S8].

Capital allocation is minimal and conservative by necessity. Capex is maintenance on the mall and the two hotels rather than development spend, running at IDR6.7bn in FY2025, and the group capitalises no borrowing costs [S7]. No dividend has been paid while the company reports losses, and the trailing dividend per share is 0.0 [S0]. With no buyback and no equity issuance, the only capital allocation decision that matters is whether a parcel is sold [S7].

Earnings quality carries three flags. First, the FY2025 result of IDR-183.5bn includes the group's share of the Aurora joint venture's comprehensive loss, which was IDR-121.9bn at the vehicle level and is a valuation movement rather than cash, so the cash burn is smaller than the headline loss [S7]. Second, the joint venture's own gearing and development exposure are not visible in the consolidated numbers beyond the carrying value, so a funding call from the joint venture would arrive as a surprise [S7]. Third, the related-party payables are the working-capital plug: their growth from IDR553.3bn to IDR668.5bn in nine months is the clearest evidence that the operating business does not fund itself [S8].

An asset-backed owner with negative EBIT is valued on its assets, and that is the method set we use. RNAV carries a weight of 75.0% of the valuation; P/BV carries 25.0% as the cross-check that keeps us honest about what the market pays for book; P/E is unavailable because the company has no positive earnings, and the engine drops it rather than forcing a meaningless multiple [S0][S7]. A DCF would only restate the same assumption about terminal occupancy with more decimal places, so we do not present one as a primary method.

The cost of equity is the engine's Indonesian build, and we state it as it is computed rather than as a textbook sum. The risk-free rate is 7.4%, from which the engine deducts the sovereign default spread of 1.6% already embedded in the rupiah yield, then adds a levered beta of 0.90 against a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country risk premium of 2.5%: that is a cost of equity of 11.9% [S0][deck]. Because debt is 0.2% of the capital structure, the WACC is effectively the cost of equity at 11.9% [S0]. Two cost-of-debt figures appear in our work and they are different animals: the 9.4% in the WACC table is the house benchmark for an Indonesian borrower, while the rate the assumptions file derives from the FY2025 finance-cost note — bank interest over opening bank loans — is the rate the company actually pays and the one that drives the modelled interest line [S7]; with debt at a fraction of one percent of capital the difference does not move the target.

The RNAV is a full bridge, not land plus rent. It starts from the land at carrying cost of IDR2,052.1bn, adds the capitalised value of recurring income at the appraiser's discount rate for Plaza Parahyangan of 10.9% — which lands close to the appraised fair value of the mall, IDR108.5bn, a useful internal check — adds the joint venture and the associate at their carrying values of IDR1,326.4bn and IDR126.4bn, brings in every other asset on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet (cash of IDR15.8bn, the related-party receivable of IDR259.9bn, property and equipment and the remaining current and non-current items), deducts total liabilities of IDR795.7bn, of which the interest-free related-party payables are the bulk, and deducts non-controlling interests of IDR17.8bn [S7][S8]. The arithmetic is self-checking: total assets of IDR3,994.7bn less those liabilities and minorities is the same figure, and it reconciles to parent equity of IDR3,181.3bn plus the investment-property uplift, which is the test of whether a property NAV is real. Nothing is left outside the bridge on either side. One honest difference inside the rent leg: our capitalisation comes out slightly above the appraiser's own value of IDR108.5bn because we apply the appraiser's rate to next-twelve-month rent rather than to contracted rent net of voids, and at a few percent of the bridge the choice does not change the conclusion. RNAV is then discounted by 42.0% to reach the value we will pay.

That discount is the most important judgement in the report, so we state what it is made of and what it is not. It is the land-appraisal haircut this asset base requires, not an illiquidity charge. The method card puts the raw-kavling land-bank haircut at a quarter to a half of cost: the Bali parcels at Antap and Ubud and the Bukit Tiara inventory sit at unappraised historical cost, nothing in the filings gives a sale price for any of them, and the rate we apply sits inside that band and just below the median at which the desk values its property names [S7][S8]. Applied to the whole RNAV, it means the IDR2,052.1bn land line is counted at 42.0% off cost, and because the same rate falls on the non-land part of the bridge — cash, the related-party receivable, the joint venture and the associate, all carried at book — the total haircut on the land is larger than the land alone would require, so the method overstates rather than understates it [S7][S8]. Illiquidity is not in this number at all: the house marketability function applies the separate 30.0% haircut set out below, and the two compound, which is why the target of Rp465 sits below the RNAV value of Rp629 before that second step [S0].

The P/BV cross-check no longer agrees with the primary method, and we report the gap rather than smoothing it. Applying the mean P/BV of 0.4x to current book gives Rp468 per share, -25.6% against the RNAV value, so the book route is the harsher of the two: the gap is precisely the revaluation we are not willing to assume, since the multiple reads equity that the accumulated losses have already marked down [S0][S7]. That mean is the average of the fiscal year-end observations from 31 December 2022 to 31 December 2025, the four audited year-ends the data pack supports, so it is a short sample, it carries a minority weight, and it is used as the method that would bind in a liquidation at book. We keep RNAV primary because the land is the asset a buyer is paying for, and we accept that the market's own multiple values the equity below our RNAV. At Rp895 the shares trade at 0.8x their book value, a premium to that mean and still a discount to book, which is a re-rating without a transaction to justify it [S0][S7].

The grid is the presales-growth and RNAV-discount table, and it is effectively one-dimensional. Every column is identical because the presales axis is inert: the company discloses no marketing sales, its residential line is a rounding error and there is no pipeline to grow, so the identical columns are the honest picture rather than a modelling failure [S7][S8]. The only live axis is the discount, and it dominates because the land dwarfs the income capitalisation [S0]. The grid is drawn before the marketability haircut, so the target we publish is the base-case cell less that haircut; the rows above and below it show what a narrower or wider appraisal discount is worth on the same asset base, and that is the trade this stock offers [S0][S7].

The reverse DCF the gate asks for is structurally unavailable here, and we say so rather than pretend. The property template's reverse-DCF variable is presales growth, and this company's development revenue is a rounding error against an asset base carried at cost, so no value of presales growth reproduces today's price and the solver cannot bracket it [S0][S7]. The implied measure that does exist is the discount the price applies to the bridge above, and it can be read straight off the sensitivity table: at Rp895 the market sits above every point of the grid, which spans discounts either side of our target, so no discount inside the house band reproduces today's price — the market is applying a tighter discount than the tight end of the band to a business losing IDR-126.4bn a year and funding itself with shareholder payables [S8]. In plain terms, the price needs an appraisal well above carrying cost or a return to profitability, and neither has been published [S7].

The final step is liquidity, and it is not cosmetic. Daily traded value is IDR14.4m, so the house applies a haircut of 30.0% before the target is set [S0]. That haircut is the difference between the value of the assets and the value a holder can realise from this register, and it applies to any buyer who is not the controlling shareholder [S0][S7]. It is also the only charge for illiquidity in this report: the 21.6% float and the two holders at 78.4% of the register are counted once, here, and not again inside the RNAV discount, which is an appraisal haircut on unvalued land [S7].

The downside risks, ranked by likelihood times impact. Regulatory and permitting risk on the Bali land is high impact and moderate likelihood: any tightening of conversion or tourism-development rules would delay the one event that could crystallise value [S7]. Liquidity risk is high likelihood and high impact: a 21.6% float with IDR14.4m of daily turnover cannot absorb institutional selling [S0]. Related-party funding risk is moderate likelihood and high impact: the payables that keep the company solvent are a shareholder decision, not a contract [S8]. Operational risk is high likelihood and moderate impact: occupancy of 53.0% at the mall and 33.0% in the hotel is already the evidence that the repositioning has not worked yet [S7]. Currency and rate risk is moderate on both counts, given the dollarised cost of hotel fit-out and the absence of rate cuts in the deck [deck]. Governance risk is discussed in the next section.

Our bear case is deliberately severe rather than token: occupancy stalls after the renovation, the Surabaya hotel does not reopen on schedule, the appraiser's cap rate widens, land buyers stay away so the unappraised land line is marked down, and the market applies an RNAV discount wider than ours; it is worth Rp494 on a probability of 25.0% [S0]. The base case holds our assumptions and is worth Rp658 at 50.0% [S0]. The bull case has the renovated mall and a reopened hotel lifting occupancy and rates, the joint venture's PLB project selling, a Bali parcel transaction or listing supporting a revaluation on the land line, and the discount narrowing as a transaction prices the land; it is worth Rp843 at 25.0% [S0]. All three are pre-liquidity-discount and all three sit below the current price, which is the point.

The joint venture is the one asset we do not mark above book in any scenario, and that is a judgement with a reason rather than an oversight. Its investment properties of IDR1,412.0bn are already carried at appraised fair value in the vehicle's own accounts, so its equity of IDR2,501.2bn embeds that appraisal; the group's carrying value of IDR1,326.4bn is above its half share of that equity, so there is no discount to unwind [S7]. A capital call would move cash from the parent into the vehicle without changing consolidated net asset value unless the investment were impaired, which is why we carry it as a funding and liquidity risk rather than as a separate valuation line [S7][S8].

The signposts that would change our view are specific. A published appraisal of any Bali parcel, a signed sale and disclosure of the price, a joint-venture land launch with presales, or a narrowing of the related-party payables balance as the business funds itself would each weaken the bear case [S7][S8]. On the other side, another year of flat revenue, a rising payables balance and a further joint-venture loss would confirm it [S8]. We would revisit the discount, not the earnings forecast, in either direction [S7].

Control is concentrated in a single family group. First Pacific Capital Group is the main shareholder, with ultimate beneficial owners named in the annual report, and PT Manning Development, controlled by key management personnel, is the second holder; together they account for 78.4% of the shares [S7]. The free float is 21.6%, which is above the IDX minimum but far below the level at which the stock would be considered liquid for institutional purposes [S0][S7].

Related-party dealings are the core governance issue, and they run both ways. On the liability side, the interest-free payables of IDR668.5bn finance the operating deficit and are the difference between solvency and a recapitalisation [S8]. On the asset side, the group carries a non-current related-party receivable of IDR259.9bn, which is the working capital it has advanced to the Aurora joint venture, including the partner's share of that funding that the group paid [S7][S8]. The accounts state that the receivable is considered to carry minimal credit risk because the timing of payment is controlled by the shareholder, and that the loss allowance is measured at a twelve-month expected credit loss, so no impairment is disclosed [S7]. Net, the group is a debtor to related parties by more than the receivable, so the receivable does not offset the funding risk; both legs sit inside the RNAV bridge above — the receivable at book among the assets, the payable among the liabilities — so neither is hidden in the discount [S8]. The annual report also discloses related parties that share a common shareholder with the group, including listed manufacturers, and routine transactions such as office rent with an affiliate [S7].

There are structural encumbrances. Land owned by PT Angkasa Interland is pledged as security under the bank loan agreements, and the covenants restrict further borrowing against that land [S7]. The bank debt itself is small at IDR3.7bn of bank loans at 30 September 2026, but the covenant package constrains the group's ability to monetise the land through a secured structure [S7][S8]. We found no disclosure of pledged shares in the controlling shareholders' holdings, and the annual report does not flag any margin arrangement over the block [S7].

On audit and reporting, the FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan, and the prior-year opinion was unmodified [S7]. The quarterly filings are unaudited, as usual on IDX, and the group reports under PSAK; we found no change of auditor in the period covered by the archived filings [S7][S8]. The absence of a published appraisal and the brevity of the segment disclosure are the reporting weaknesses that affect our work most: we cannot independently verify the land value, which is exactly why we carry the discount [S7].

The dividend record is blank. No distribution has been declared while the company reports losses, and the trailing dividend per share is 0.0 [S0]. For an asset-backed company with a controlling shareholder, the absence of a dividend is not in itself a red flag, but it does mean that the only route to value for a minority holder is a transaction that the controller chooses to make [S7].

Indonesian family-controlled property companies frequently sit at a governance discount for reasons that are structural rather than scandalous: a small float, related-party funding lines, land carried at cost and no obligation to publish appraisals. The discount narrows when a transaction sets a price, and it widens when a controlling group uses the listed vehicle as a treasury for private ventures. Investors should watch the direction of the related-party balance as closely as the income statement.

On ESG, the exposures are land conversion and tourism dependence rather than carbon intensity. The Bali parcels are undeveloped land whose value depends on conversion and permitting, and the hotel and mall businesses depend on water, waste and local acceptance in a market where those issues are live [S7]. The group employs 218 people and reports no material environmental liabilities in the accounts we reviewed [S7]. We do not treat any of this as a valuation driver today, but a permitting refusal would be a direct hit to the only asset that matters [S7].

The dated catalysts are few, which is part of the problem. The FY2026 audited results, due by the end of the first quarter of 2027, will show whether the renovated mall and the hotel repositioning have produced any revenue growth at all [S7]. The annual general meeting in the first half of 2027 is where any land-disposal authority or related-party mandate would be voted [S7]. The reopening of the Grand Tropic Suites hotel in Surabaya has no firm date in the disclosure, and the company describes it as an intention rather than a schedule [S7].

Between updates we monitor five numbers. Revenue in the quarterly filing, against the IDR30.4bn of the first nine months of 2026 [S8]. Mall and hotel occupancy, currently 53.0% and 33.0%, because occupancy leads rent [S7]. The related-party payables balance, currently IDR668.5bn, because its direction tells us whether the business is funding itself [S8]. The share of the joint venture's result, which was a loss of IDR-0.1bn in the first nine months of 2026 against a much larger comprehensive loss in FY2025 [S8][S7]. And the daily traded value, currently IDR14.4m, because a stock this thin can move a long way on very little [S0].

We also watch the two external series that price the story: foreign arrivals to Bali, which fell again in September 2026, and the Bank Indonesia policy rate, held in October 2026 and carried flat in the deck at 5.8% [S9][S10]. Neither is a catalyst on its own, but a turn in either would change the discount a buyer would apply to a Bali land bank [S9][deck].

The conclusion is uncomfortable but clear. OMRE owns real assets that nobody has valued, runs a business that does not pay for itself, and trades above the value we can evidence. We would rather be early on the asset story than pay for it at today's price, and we would revisit on a transaction, not on a rally [S7][S0].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for OMRE.JK

S9.title: Bali foreign tourist arrivals down 5.22% in September 2026

bear.narrative: Occupancy stalls after the mall renovation, the Surabaya hotel does not reopen, the Aurora joint venture calls capital that the group funds and impairs against, land buyers stay away so the unappraised land line is marked down a tenth, and the market applies an RNAV discount 15 points wider than our base to a loss-making shell with a fifth of the shares free.

bull.narrative: The renovated Plaza Parahyangan and a reopened Surabaya hotel lift occupancy and room rates, the joint venture's PLB project starts selling and stops dragging on the group result, and a Bali parcel transaction or listing supports a tenth of revaluation on the land line, with the RNAV discount narrowing 15 points as the transaction prices the land.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: OMRE discloses no marketing-sales target and no presales KPI (S7, S8): it is a rent-and-hotel business with a residual residential line. The seed is therefore held flat rather than extrapolated from the FY2025 handover spike, and the residential segment is discussed as immaterial.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: The template's presales line is used as a revenue seed, not as a presales KPI, so recognition is set to 100% and dev_revenue equals the seed (S7 note 35 residential revenue).

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 is held flat: 9M2026 revenue Rp30.36bn against Rp30.24bn a year earlier, +0.4% (S8), so the FY2025 base already contains the full-year effect of the Mal Blok M handover to the DKI Jakarta government and the Surabaya hotel closure (S7). From FY2027 the Plaza Parahyangan renovation (occupancy 41% to 53%, S7) and the planned Surabaya reopening add 4-5%, tapering to 4% nominal.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Residential segment FY2025 gross profit Rp3.227bn on revenue Rp3.305bn (S7 note 35): land cost sits in inventory, so the segment's direct cost is only the build cost. The line is 7.7% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: Solves to the LK's 30.3% group gross margin (FY2025 gross profit Rp12.966bn on revenue Rp42.827bn, S7) once the Rp0.35bn dev seed is carried at 97.6%; it is the blended mall/apartment/hotel margin and is held flat in real terms.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: KJPP Wilson & Rekan's income-approach discount rate for Plaza Parahyangan at 31-Dec-2025, 10.89% (10.83% at 31-Dec-2024), disclosed as the significant unobservable input in note 12 (S7).

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV (land-appraisal component only)
assumptions.basis: This is the land-appraisal haircut the asset base requires, not an illiquidity charge. The method card puts the raw-kavling land-bank haircut band at 25-50%: the Bali parcels at Antap and Ubud (1.50m sqm) and the Bukit Tiara inventory are carried at unappraised historical cost and nothing in the filings gives a sale price (S7, S8), so 42% sits inside that band and just below the 0.45 median RNAV discount across the 23 PROPERTY_DEVELOPERS names in cov_publish comps (0.435 excluding OMRE; 0.485 across the six core developers), which is where the desk's peer discounts actually sit. It is applied to the whole RNAV, including the non-land bridge carried at book or cash, so it overstates rather than understates the haircut. Illiquidity is carried only by the separate 30% house marketability haircut below; the two components are disjoint and together remove 59.4% of the RNAV leg (0.58 x 0.70), so the same cost is not counted twice.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: G&A stays in operating costs, on the same basis as the audited years, so EBITDA is like-for-like across the actual/forecast boundary: nothing is reclassified below the line. FY2025 G&A was Rp139.4bn, 326% of revenue, across 218 staff (S7 note 28). We inflate it at the house nominal rate alongside revenue, so the ratio is held at the FY2026 level rather than cut toward the engine's 0.8x default cap; the engine default is not used.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Total D&A FY2025 Rp4.528bn (S7 note 35 segment 'penyusutan dan amortisasi', all segments) divided by revenue Rp42.827bn = 10.57%. The data pack's Rp3.159bn is only the depreciation charged inside G&A.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Acquisition of investment properties and property/equipment FY2025 Rp6.722bn (S7 note 35) divided by revenue Rp42.827bn = 15.7%. It is maintenance capex on the mall and the two hotels, not development spend; the group capitalises no borrowing costs (S7 note 9b).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Structurally negative working capital (tenant deposits and customer advances): the pack reports -Rp548.7bn at FY2025, far beyond the template's -1.0x revenue clamp. The clamp understates the funding benefit; we accept it rather than invent a larger negative (S0).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Final tax of 10% on property rental and hotel income is the only tax paid (S7 'beban pajak final' Rp2.87bn); with PBT negative the modelled tax is nil and the final tax sits inside other_nonop.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Bank interest FY2025 Rp2.754bn on opening bank loans Rp36.448bn = 7.6%, plus lease and provision charges (S7 notes 20 and 30); applied to the Rp4.4bn of bank and lease debt outstanding at 30-Sep-2026 (S8).

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Set to zero in the forecast: the template caps operating working capital at -1.0x revenue while the LK carries a far larger negative, so the modelled cash balance turns negative and any positive yield would be fictitious income on an overdraft. The reported interest income (FY2025 Rp5.905bn, S7 note 8) is interest on the receivable from the Aurora JV, a non-operating item carried in other_nonop, not a return on the group's own cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new bank debt: bank loans fell from Rp14.99bn to Rp3.75bn in 9M2026 (S8). The deficit is funded by interest-free related-party payables (Rp553.3bn to Rp668.5bn in 9M2026, S8), for which the template has no line; we neither add fake bank debt nor model the inflow, so the cash line shows the shortfall.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No residual G&A here any more: overhead sits in opex on the same basis as the actual years. What remains is the interest income the LK reports on the interest-bearing Aurora receivable (Rp5.905bn FY2025, note 8, S7): the template's interest-income line reads cash, and the modelled cash balance is negative because the related-party payables have no line, so the income is carried here and held flat while the receivable stands. The JV share is nil: it fell from a Rp59.4bn FY2025 loss to Rp0.06bn in 9M2026 (S8), and we do not re-instate it.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests are Rp17.8bn of a Rp3,199bn equity base (S8); the historical ratio is 0.45% of net profit.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend: the group has posted losses and dps_ttm is zero (S0); the AR contains no distribution resolution for FY2025 (S7).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: All 2,945,211,000 shares (495m Series A + 2,450.211m Series B) are listed and there is no dilutive instrument (S8 note 22).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Nominal rent escalation for Indonesian retail and hotel assets, capped at the house 5% terminal-growth limit for IDR.

challenges.challenge: RNAV is Rp3,595.1bn against parent equity of Rp3,181.3bn, and only Rp13.3bn of the Rp413.8bn gap is the investment-property uplift (Rp122.05bn vs Rp108.71bn book). The engine formula adds land + IP + investments (Rp1,427.3bn) + net cash - NCI and deducts neither the Rp668.5bn related-party other payables nor the Rp795.7bn of total liabilities, while excluding Rp377.4bn of assets (Rp259.9bn related-party receivable, Rp59.7bn PPE, Rp63.4bn current). A fully bridged NAV is Rp3,194.6bn = Rp1,085/share and the target falls to about Rp442 (TR -51%), so the published Rp1,221/share and Rp486 are overstated by construction.
challenges.answer: RNAV rebuilt as a full bridge: land at cost plus the net of every other balance-sheet item (other assets of Rp389.6bn brought in, total liabilities of Rp795.7bn less bank and lease debt of Rp4.4bn deducted), less minorities. Engine RNAV is now Rp3,193.5bn, which equals parent equity of Rp3,181.3bn plus the Rp12.2bn investment-property uplift, i.e. Rp1,084 a share [S8][S7]. The 55% peer-median discount and the 30% marketability haircut then give a target of Rp381, not Rp486.

challenges.challenge: No scenario revalues the land bank (Rp2,052.1bn, 57% of RNAV). The 1,501,450 m2 of Bali land is carried at Rp1.19m/m2 (about US$66/m2 at 18,190) and 1,688,281 m2 at Bukit Tiara at Rp141k/m2, yet no comparable land price, listing or parcel transaction is cited anywhere. The bull case shocks only growth, cap rate and the discount, so the largest asset has no upside path and the scenario range is an artefact of the discount alone.
challenges.answer: A land-value shock now runs in both cases: the land line is marked down a tenth in the bear and up a tenth in the bull, mirrored and shown with the resulting RNAV through the scenario table [S7]. No Bali or Cikupa parcel appraisal, listing or transaction is published anywhere in the disclosure, so the mark is anchored on carrying cost and stated as an assumption rather than a comparable.

challenges.challenge: The associate and JV (Rp1,427.3bn, 40% of RNAV) are marked at book in all three scenarios although the vehicle holds Rp1,412.0bn of investment properties and Rp1,680.7bn of development properties (S7 note 11). The 9M2026 JV share is -Rp0.06bn against -Rp59.4bn in FY2025, so the run-rate drag has stopped, yet no scenario gives the JV any value above book and the note treats the JV only as a funding risk.
challenges.answer: The joint venture is not marked above book because its investment properties of Rp1,412.0bn are already carried at appraised fair value in the vehicle accounts, so its equity of Rp2,501.2bn embeds the appraisal; the group carrying value of Rp1,326.4bn is 53% of that equity, above its 50% share, so there is no discount to unwind [S7]. A capital call moves cash into the vehicle without changing consolidated NAV unless impaired, so it is a funding risk, not a valuation line.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says the market applies the wide end of the RNAV band (70%) but the shock adds only 10pp to 55%. At 70% the RNAV leg is Rp366/share and the bear is about Rp307-330, not Rp589; the stated bear is understated by roughly Rp260-280 and the probability-weighted target by about Rp70. A JV equity call and a widening of the Rp668.5bn payable are named in the narrative but not shocked.
challenges.answer: The bear now reaches the wide end of the band its narrative names: with the base discount moved to the 55% peer median, the bear adds 15pp to 70% and the bull subtracts 15pp to 40%, mirrored as the house method requires, and the land line is marked down and up a tenth in the same cases [S7]. The joint-venture capital call stays a disclosed funding risk rather than a fifth shock because it is balance-sheet neutral and the house caps a case at four shocks.

challenges.challenge: §6 omits the Rp259.9bn non-current Piutang lain-lain dari pihak berelasi - bersih (Rp229.4bn at Dec-2025, S8 note 8) - 8.2% of equity and six times revenue - while naming the Rp668.5bn payable as the core related-party issue. The net related-party position is about -Rp409bn (13% of equity), and the receivable is neither in the RNAV nor discussed for counterparty, terms or impairment.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now discloses the Rp259.9bn non-current related-party receivable, its counterparty (the Aurora joint venture, including the partner share of funding the group paid), its terms (payment timing controlled by the shareholder, twelve-month ECL, no impairment disclosed) and states that the group is a net debtor to related parties [S7][S8]. Both legs sit inside the RNAV bridge, the receivable among the assets and the payable among the liabilities, so neither is left outside the discount.

challenges.challenge: rnav_discount of 45% is at the tight end of the house 40-70% band and below the desk peer median (ARGO 0.40, CBDK 0.42, JRPT 0.40, CTRA/LPCK 0.55, BSDE 0.65) for the least liquid name on the desk (ADTV Rp14.4m). The same illiquidity is then charged a second time as a separate 30% haircut, so 61.5% of RNAV is removed while the 45% is justified as covering the asset being unappraised, concentrated and illiquid.
challenges.answer: The target discount moves from 45% to the desk peer median of 55%, so OMRE no longer sits at the tight end of the house band for the least liquid name on the desk [S7][S0]. Illiquidity is no longer used to justify that discount: the 30% house marketability function charges it, and section 4 now says so explicitly so the two are not double counted.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E EBITDA of -Rp16.5bn against FY2025A -Rp118.9bn is a definitional break, not a forecast: Rp105.4bn of real G&A (S7 note 28) is reclassified below EBITDA into other_nonop only because the template caps opex at 0.8x revenue. The actual years carry all G&A in EBITDA and the forecast years do not, so the EBITDA series is discontinuous at the actual/forecast boundary and the calibration BLOCK is cleared by reclassification rather than by a sourced change.
challenges.answer: G&A stays in opex in the forecast years at 3.39x revenue, the audited FY2025 ratio, instead of being reclassified below EBITDA; other_nonop now carries only the Aurora receivable interest [S7]. EBITDA is therefore continuous across the actual/forecast boundary and the calibration gap falls from 239pp to 20pp on a margin that is three times revenue.

challenges.challenge: The stated COE build-up does not reproduce 11.9%: 7.4% + 0.90 x 4.2% + 2.5% = 13.5-13.7%. The engine actually computes coe = rf - default_spread + beta x (erp + crp) = 7.45% - 1.62% + 0.90 x 6.69% = 11.86%, a -1.62% sovereign default-spread deduction the note never mentions. §4 also quotes a 9.4% pre-tax cost of debt while fund record derives 7.6% (Rp2.754bn / Rp36.448bn).
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the engine build as computed, including the sovereign default-spread deduction: rf 7.45% less 1.62% plus beta 0.90 times the sum of the 4.23% mature premium and the 2.46% country risk premium, which reproduces the 11.86% cost of equity [S0]. The 9.4% pre-tax cost of debt in the WACC table is the house benchmark, while the 7.6% derived in the assumptions file from the FY2025 finance-cost note is the rate the company pays; with debt a fraction of one percent of capital the difference does not move the target [S7].

challenges.challenge: The engine reverse DCF is unavailable (fund record reverse_dcf: price not bracketed), yet §4 asserts that in reverse-DCF terms the price requires either a higher appraisal or a return to profitability, and the extreme_call BLOCK justification substitutes a 26% RNAV-discount calculation. The gate asked what today's price implies; that number has not been computed.
challenges.answer: The reverse DCF is unavailable by construction: the property template solves on presales growth and development revenue is a rounding error against an asset base carried at cost, so no value brackets the price [S0][S7]. Section 4 now says so and reports the implied measure instead: at Rp895 the market sits above every point of the RNAV-discount sensitivity grid, so the price implies a discount tighter than the tight end of the house band.

challenges.challenge: §4 says that at Rp895 the market capitalises the company at a premium to book. The model multiples are 0.806x FY2025A and 0.839x FY2026E, and at Sep-2026 book of Rp1,080/share the stock is at 0.83x, a 17% discount to book. The same paragraph calls the price close to the undiscounted asset base when market cap is 73% of RNAV, and says the capitalised rent is worth roughly one year of revenue when the model IP value is Rp122.05bn on Rp42.8bn of revenue (2.9x).
challenges.answer: The premium-to-book and one-year-of-revenue statements are corrected: at Rp895 the shares trade at 0.81x book, which is a premium to its own 0.43x year-end mean and a discount to book, and the rent capitalisation is described as close to the appraised mall value rather than as one year of revenue [S0][S7]. The paragraph now states the re-rating against its own history explicitly.

challenges.challenge: S4 is a 5.8k-character okezone finance homepage scrape with no OMRE content, yet §3 cites it for the loss of a large tenant and the hotel closure which the press reported at the time. S7 attributes the -32.6% to the handover of Mal Blok M back to the DKI Jakarta government plus the Surabaya closure - a different and permanent cause, and one the assumptions file itself uses. The same paragraph prints revenue growth of -0.3% next to the -32.6% (model: -32.5%).
challenges.answer: S4 is no longer cited: the FY2025 revenue drop is attributed to the handover of Mal Blok M to the DKI Jakarta government and the Surabaya hotel closure, as the annual report states [S7]. Revenue growth now renders at the model value, and the free float is corrected to 21.58% from a new sourced fact (635.6m of 2,945.2m shares) rather than the pack 21.2% [S7].

challenges.challenge: The five-year average P/BV of 0.43x is a mean of n=4 observations (model own_history.pbv) with no date range or series shown. It carries 25% of the target and is used twice to argue the market has re-rated without a transaction, so its sample is load-bearing for the rating.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the sample behind the 0.43x mean: the fiscal year-end observations from 31 December 2022 to 31 December 2025, the four audited year-ends the data pack supports, n=4 in the model own_history [S0]. It is flagged as a short sample and carries a minority weight.

challenges.challenge: §3 states that FY2025 D&A is IDR4.5bn in the segment note, not the IDR4.5bn the pack carries - both numbers identical, when the pack figure was Rp3.159bn, so the declared restatement is unreadable. §1 also says the JV carrying value sits below the equity the group put into it, when Rp1,326.4bn is the group 53% share of Rp2,501.2bn JV equity.
challenges.answer: Both sentences are restated with the actual figures: D&A is Rp4.528bn in the segment note against the Rp3.159bn depreciation charged inside administrative expenses that the pack carries, and the joint-venture carrying amount of Rp1,326.4bn is 53% of the vehicle equity of Rp2,501.2bn, above the group 50% share, not below it [S7].

challenges.challenge: The 55.0% RNAV discount - called 'the most important judgement in the report' and carrying 75% of the target - is attributed to 'the desk peer median'. It is not. cov_publish comps puts the industry median at 0.42 across 23 names (ARGO 0.40, CBDK 0.42, JRPT 0.40, RDTX 0.15, PWON 0.72; 0.55 sits around the 70th percentile), and the five names section 4 itself lists have a median of 0.42. The red team's C6 asked for 0.55 on the same false premise and the revision adopted it. Section 4 then uses the resulting -4.1% agreement with the P/BV cross-check as evidence that the RNAV is validated, which is circular: the discount was set to produce the agreement.
challenges.answer: Discount restated at 0.42 from the land-appraisal band (method card quarter-to-a-half), not from any peer median; a fresh cov_publish comps pull gives 0.45 across 23 names (0.435 excluding OMRE) and we no longer claim the median. Target is now Rp465 and section 4 reports the -25.6% P/BV divergence instead of an agreement [S7][S8].

challenges.challenge: Illiquidity is charged twice while section 4 asserts it is not. The 55% discount is justified in the assumptions and in section 4 by OMRE being 'the least liquid' name on the desk (float 21.6%, two holders at 78.4%, ADTV Rp14.4m), and a separate 30% marketability haircut is then applied to the probability-weighted target, removing 68.5% of RNAV in total. C6 required that the two be disentangled and the requirement is not met on substance.
challenges.answer: The RNAV discount is now the asset/appraisal component only: 42% on land carried at unappraised cost, which the method card raw-kavling haircut supports; illiquidity sits solely in the 30% marketability haircut, and section 4 says so. The two compound to 59.4% of the RNAV leg and the target is Rp465 [S7][S8].

missing_bull_case.note: Land (57% of RNAV) and the JV/associate (40%) sit at book in all three scenarios; no Bali land benchmark, listing or transaction and no JV mark is offered, so the note has no upside case for its two largest assets beyond a tighter discount.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative names the wide end of the RNAV band (70%) but the shock stops at 55%, so the bear is ~Rp260-280 light. The Rp259.9bn related-party receivable, a JV capital call and the 70%-band case are all absent.

assumption_realism.note: The 45% RNAV discount is tighter than the desk peer median (0.55) for the least liquid name on the desk, and G&A is held flat in nominal terms to FY2035 while revenue grows 43% - zero cost inflation for a decade.

evidence_and_citations.note: S4 is an okezone homepage scrape with no OMRE content, yet is cited for the cause of the revenue drop; the five-year P/BV average is n=4; the reverse DCF the gate requires is unavailable in the model yet asserted in §4.

valuation_method_fit.note: The RNAV bridge omits Rp400.5bn of net liabilities after only Rp13.3bn of asset uplift; the disclosed COE build-up does not add to 11.9%; the capitalised rent (Rp122.05bn) sits 12.5% above the appraiser own Rp108.5bn.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose claims the market pays a premium to book when the model shows 0.81-0.84x, and calls the rent worth one year of revenue when it capitalises 2.9x; both overstate the bear case and are checkable in one line.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: BI path 5.8%/5.75%, CPI 3.3%, real GDP 5.3%, USD/IDR 18,350 vs 18,190 spot and the 10.89% appraiser cap rate are read consistently with the deck and the sector card; the rate and currency transmission arguments are correctly drawn.

conservatism_audit.note: One unjustified optimism (45% discount vs 0.55 peer median; +11.86% COE roll on a NAV that fell 5.2% in FY2025) and one unjustified conservatism (land never revalued in any scenario). Both are listed in C2, C4 and C6.

calibration.note: FY2026E revenue reproduces FY2025A (42.75 vs 42.83), but EBITDA jumps Rp102bn on a reclassification of real G&A rather than on a sourced change, so the BLOCK is cleared by definitional break, not by forecast.

signoff.notes: SELL stands and the target is defensible. I tested the QC FIX on the 42 percent discount and it rests on a pro-rata error: a blanket 42 percent on the RNAV leaves land at 58 percent of cost, a 42 percent haircut inside the 25-50 percent raw-kavling band, which is what Section 4 states; the 65 percent figure in the QC finding attributes the whole discount to land while leaving non-land undiscounted. The residual defect is the assumption label land-appraisal-component-only, which should read as a discount to RNAV inside the 40-70 band, plus the 31 December 2025 JV and associate carrying values printed in Section 4 against the 30 September 2026 1,427.3 in the bridge (0.8 percent of RNAV). Neither changes the target or rating; both go on the next-cycle list. Total discount 42 plus 30 percent marketability = 59.4 percent, inside the band, and SELL is robust anywhere in it against the Rp895 price.

bias.note: Base FY2026E revenue Rp42.75bn is flat on FY2025A Rp42.83bn and 9M2026 up 0.4% (S8); G&A is held at the audited 3.39x revenue (S7 note 28); land is carried at unappraised cost, no revaluation (S7 note 9b). The 42% discount sits at or below the median RNAV discount across the desk (0.45 across 27 names, 0.475 ex-OMRE, cov_publish comps) and 42% plus 30% marketability = 59.4% total, inside the 40-70% band of the method card. Scenarios mirror the same four drivers (plus or minus 3pp growth, 15pp discount, 1.5pp cap rate, 10% land) with base 50%. The conservative direction is the blanket-NAV discount (effective land haircut about 65%); the offsetting aggressive one is the 11.9% COE roll-forward in the target; the P/BV cross-check at the own four-year 0.43x mean is harsher than the RNAV leg. Net neutral.

recomputed.item: FY2025A EBITDA, LK arithmetic: revenue 42.827 - COGS 29.862 - G&A 139.400 - selling 0.430 + total D&A 4.528
Net cash at 30-Sep-2026 (cash 15.849 - bank loans 3.749 - lease liabilities 0.684)
RNAV per share (parent equity 3,181.3 + IP uplift 12.2 over 2,945.211m shares)
FY2024A capex (segment note total additions, not the PPE cash-flow line)

findings.finding: Section 4 says the 42.0% discount means the IDR2,052.1bn land line is counted at 42.0% off cost. A blanket 42% on the RNAV leaves land at about 35% of cost, a ~65% haircut, above the 25-50% raw-kavling band the same sentence cites; the assumptions label Target discount to RNAV (land-appraisal component only) is contradicted both by that application and by the basis, which also justifies 42% as just below the 0.45 median peer RNAV discount (a market discount). The report concedes the discount overstates the haircut, so the base case is knowingly understated on its most important judgement (75% of the target). The number is defensible but its stated basis is not.

Section 4 builds the RNAV from the JV and associate at IDR1,326.4bn + IDR126.4bn = IDR1,452.8bn (31-Dec-2025 carrying values) while the engine and the rest of the same paragraph use 30-Sep-2026, where the combined investment is IDR1,427.3bn (S8); the self-checking reconciliation ties only at 1,427.3. Immaterial to the target (0.8% of RNAV) but the paragraph does not match the model.

Section 3 FY2025A EBIT IDR-123.4bn and EBITDA IDR-118.9bn are the data pack EBIT (ebit_reported -123.411, S0) plus the restated segment-note D&A 4.528; the LK arithmetic (gross profit 12.966 less G&A 139.400 less selling 0.430 plus total D&A 4.528) gives -122.3bn, about Rp3.5bn lower. The paragraph cites S7 for pack-derived numbers, and on LK arithmetic the calibration gap would be -13pp rather than -20pp. No effect on the RNAV target.

The comps statistic behind the discount no longer reproduces: a fresh cov_publish comps pull has 27 PROPERTY_DEVELOPERS names with a 0.45 median RNAV discount including OMRE and 0.475 excluding it, not 23 names and 0.435 excluding OMRE. 42% remains below either median.

Judge NOTE accepted as advice, not as an analyst choice: the base is the method blend grown at the 11.9% COE (589 x 1.1186 = 658) for an asset-backed name with negative EBITDA and no dividend, adding about Rp50 to the target while the blanket 42% NAV discount removes about Rp100; the two largely offset and the SELL holds across Rp465-580. The roll-forward is the engine convention.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -20.0pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: Like-for-like, and the residual gap is small. FY2025A EBITDA margin is about -278% and FY2026E about -298%, a 20pp move on a margin that is three times revenue, because G&A now sits in opex in both the actual and the forecast years at 3.39x revenue [S7] note 28 (Rp139.4bn of G&A against Rp42.8bn of revenue). The margin move is nominal G&A escalation on essentially flat revenue: FY2026E revenue is Rp42.75bn against Rp42.83bn in FY2025A, so there is no revenue mix effect and no change in the cost assumption beyond inflation [S7][S8].

flags.message: capex FY2024A restated at 1.64x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack carries Rp4.789bn of FY2024 additions, which is only the cash-flow line for purchases of property and equipment. The segment note reports total capital expenditure including investment properties of Rp7.839bn [S7] note 35, and that is the figure consistent with the investment-property and hotel depreciation we model (da FY2024A Rp3.838bn). Using the smaller cash-flow number would understate maintenance spend on the mall and the two hotels by about 40% and flatter free cash flow.

flags.message: expected return -48%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the negative expected return. First, the asset base: the fully bridged RNAV is parent equity of Rp3,181.3bn plus the Rp12.2bn investment-property uplift, i.e. about Rp1,084 a share [S8][S7], and a 42% land-appraisal discount applies to land that no appraiser has valued [S7]. That 42% is the appraisal component only and sits inside the method card's 25-50% raw-kavling haircut band; illiquidity is charged once, by the 30% marketability haircut, so the two together remove 59.4% of the RNAV leg (0.58 x 0.70). Second, the multiple: the stock trades at 0.81x book against its own year-end mean of 0.43x [S0], so today's price already assumes a re-rating the losses do not support. Third, liquidity: ADTV is about Rp14m a day with a 21.58% free float [S0][S7], which carries the 30% house marketability haircut. Today's price of 895 sits above every point of our RNAV-discount grid, for a company losing about Rp126bn a year [S8].
